description.summary: Fixed-Size Chunking splits source content into uniform windows so ingestion can produce predictable retrieval units.
description.description: Fixed-Size Chunking is a RAG technique that divides source content into character, token, or approximate-size windows before embedding, indexing, or retrieval.
description.problemStatement: A RAG pipeline needs content units that are small enough to index and retrieve, but source documents may be too large or irregular for direct use.
description.coreIdea: Split content into deterministic windows with a configured size and optional overlap so downstream stages receive consistent chunk artifacts.

inputRequirements.name: Source content
inputRequirements.description: Documents or text content that should be divided into retrieval-ready chunks.

outputArtifacts.name: Fixed-size chunks
outputArtifacts.description: Uniform or approximately uniform content windows prepared for embedding or indexing.

implementationConsiderations: Choose chunk size and overlap deliberately because boundary cuts can reduce semantic coherence.
Use fixed-size chunks as a simple deterministic baseline before adopting more complex chunking strategies.
evaluationGuidance: Compare retrieval quality across chunk sizes and overlap settings using the same corpus and retrieval configuration.
